title: 2024 AMC 10A Problem 3
statement: What is the sum of the digits of the smallest prime that can be written as a sum of \(5\) distinct primes?

solutions.text: Suppose \(2\) is one of the five primes. Then the total is even and bigger than \(2,\) so it is composite. Thus all five primes must be odd. The five smallest odd primes give \(3 + 5 + 7 + 11 + 13 = 39\) \(= 3 \cdot 13,\) which is not prime. The next possible sum is obtained by replacing \(13\) with the next prime, \(17;\) changing any earlier term forces at least as large an increase to keep the primes distinct. This gives \(3 + 5 + 7 + 11 + 17 = 43,\) which is prime. Its digit sum is \(4 + 3 = 7.\) Thus, B is the correct answer.
hints: Using \(2\) makes the sum even and larger than \(2,\) so it cannot be prime; use five odd primes
The five smallest odd primes sum to \(39,\) which is not prime; increase to the next prime sum
